posts.source: Nov 10 Hanzi Threads lesson record (text intent)
posts.body:
Someone asks for a decision while you’re still reading the message. Try buying a moment:

我需要一点时间。
Wǒ xūyào yìdiǎn shíjiān.
I need a little time.

一点 (yìdiǎn) means “a little” here.

posts.label: Nov 11, 7:00 PM
posts.source: The last dumpling (prepared Hanzi story theme, video review only)
posts.body:
Mini-fable: Two sparrows guarded the last dumpling. A third brought a knife. Suddenly there were three bites.

我们分着吃吧。
Wǒmen fēnzhe chī ba.
Let’s share it.

分着吃 (fēnzhe chī) means to divide something up and eat it together.

posts.label: Nov 12, 9:00 AM
posts.source: The last dumpling (related original dining-language follow-up)
posts.body:
At a shared meal, a host might say:

再吃一点吧。
Zài chī yìdiǎn ba.
Have a little more.

再 (zài) adds the idea of another helping. If you’re full, try 我吃饱了 (Wǒ chī bǎo le): “I’m full.”
